questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A multinational enterprise manages 200 AWS accounts governed by AWS Control Tower. The engineering organization requires an automated infrastructure-as-code (IaC) pipeline to provision new accounts with pre-configured VPCs, security baselines, IAM roles, and centralized logging. The pipeline must integrate natively with an enterprise Terraform Cloud repository, trigger automated deployments upon account creation requests, and ensure consistent multi-account customization without requiring manual console configuration. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda function in the management account triggered by CloudWatch Events to call the CreateAccount API and execute local shell scripts containing Terraform binary CLI commands on a self-managed EC2 instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed EC2 execution servers with custom shell scripts create single points of failure, scaling bottlenecks, and severe operational maintenance overhead.

options.text: Deploy the AWS Control Tower Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) framework, configuring the Git repository for account requests and pipeline customizations to automatically provision and baseline new accounts using Terraform Cloud.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Control Tower Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) is the AWS-recommended solution for automating account provisioning, baselining, and customization using Terraform pipelines.

options.text: Create an AWS Service Catalog portfolio containing AWS CloudFormation templates in every member account and instruct account administrators to launch products manually via the AWS Management Console.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Manual execution in each member account fails the automated Git-driven pipeline requirement and introduces high administrative complexity.

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule in each member account that triggers AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks to compile and execute local Terraform state files from an S3 bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Distributing Terraform state management across hundreds of standalone member accounts without a central orchestrator creates synchronization conflicts and lacks unified governance.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Control Tower Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) integrates Terraform pipelines directly with AWS Control Tower, automatically provisioning and customizing new AWS accounts in response to Git repository requests.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An enterprise connects an on-premises data center with 120 AWS VPCs via an AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. The company maintains an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory DNS infrastructure (example.corp) while hosting internal cloud microservices within Route 53 private hosted zones (aws.internal). On-premises corporate workstations must resolve aws.internal records, and Amazon EC2 instances across all 120 VPCs must seamlessly resolve example.corp hostnames. The architecture must centralize DNS resolution management in a Shared-Services VPC and minimize DNS query latency and operational overhead. Which solution should the architect implement?

options.text: Deploy custom BIND DNS forwarder EC2 instances in every one of the 120 VPCs, configuring local iptables forwarding rules to synchronize DNS caches with on-premises domain controllers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying and maintaining 120 pairs of self-managed BIND forwarders requires substantial patching, monitoring, high-availability management, and licensing overhead.

options.text: Create Route 53 public hosted zones for both example.corp and aws.internal, creating public A records for all internal microservices and securing endpoints using AWS WAF IP sets.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exposing internal corporate domain names and private IP addresses in public DNS hosted zones creates major security vulnerabilities and violates internal corporate data confidentiality.

options.text: Deploy Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints in the Shared-Services VPC to receive queries from on-premises DNS forwarders for aws.internal. Deploy Route 53 Resolver Outbound Endpoints in the Shared-Services VPC with a forwarding rule for example.corp pointing to on-premises DNS IPs, and share the rule across all 120 VPCs using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
options.explanation: Correct: Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints allow on-premises clients to resolve AWS private hosted zones, while Outbound Endpoints with RAM-shared forwarding rules allow all VPCs to resolve on-premises domains seamlessly without per-VPC server management.

options.text: Configure VPC Peering between all 120 VPCs and the on-premises network, and set DHCP Option Sets in all VPCs to point directly to the on-premises Active Directory DNS server IP addresses.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Pointing VPC DHCP option sets directly to on-premises DNS servers causes AWS services (such as EC2 instance metadata 169.254.169.254 and VPC-provided Route 53 endpoints) to fail resolution.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints (for on-premises to AWS DNS queries) and Outbound Endpoints with Resolver Rules shared via AWS RAM (for AWS to on-premises DNS forwarding) in a central Shared-Services VPC fulfills bidirectional hybrid resolution with centralized management.

pt.domainName: Domínio 1: Projetar Soluções para Complexidade Organizacional
pt.statement: Uma empresa conecta um data center on-premises com 120 VPCs na AWS via uma conexão dedicada do AWS Direct Connect. A empresa mantém uma infraestrutura de DNS Microsoft Active Directory on-premises (example.corp) enquanto hospeda microsserviços internos na nuvem em zonas hospedadas privadas do Route 53 (aws.internal). Estações de trabalho corporativas on-premises devem resolver registros de aws.internal, e instâncias Amazon EC2 em todas as 120 VPCs devem resolver perfeitamente nomes de host de example.corp. A arquitetura deve centralizar o gerenciamento de resolução de DNS em uma VPC de Serviços Compartilhados e minimizar a latência de consultas e sobrecarga operacional. Qual solução o arquiteto deve implementar?

options.text: Implantar instâncias EC2 com encaminhadores de DNS BIND customizados em cada uma das 120 VPCs, configurando regras locais de iptables para sincronizar caches de DNS com os controladores de domínio on-premises.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Implantar e manter 120 pares de servidores BIND autogerenciados exige aplicação contínua de patches, monitoramento, gestão de alta disponibilidade e alta sobrecarga operacional.

options.text: Criar zonas hospedadas públicas do Route 53 para example.corp e aws.internal, criando registros A públicos para todos os microsserviços internos e protegendo endpoints usando IP sets do AWS WAF.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Expor nomes de domínio corporativos internos e endereços IP privados em zonas DNS públicas cria graves vulnerabilidades de segurança e viola a confidencialidade de dados da empresa.

options.text: Implantar Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints na VPC de Serviços Compartilhados para receber consultas de encaminhadores DNS on-premises para aws.internal. Implantar Outbound Endpoints na VPC de Serviços Compartilhados com uma regra de encaminhamento para example.corp apontando para IPs on-premises, compartilhando a regra com as 120 VPCs via AWS RAM.
options.explanation: Correto: Os Inbound Endpoints do Route 53 Resolver permitem que clientes on-premises resolvam zonas privadas da AWS, enquanto Outbound Endpoints com regras compartilhadas via RAM permitem que todas as VPCs resolvam domínios on-premises sem gerenciar servidores adicionais.

options.text: Configurar VPC Peering entre todas as 120 VPCs e a rede on-premises e definir DHCP Option Sets em todas as VPCs apontando diretamente para os endereços IP dos servidores DNS do Active Directory on-premises.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Apontar DHCP Option Sets diretamente para servidores DNS on-premises faz com que a resolução de nomes de endpoints internos da AWS (como metadados de instância 169.254.169.254 e DNS nativo da VPC) falhe.

pt.generalExplanation: A implantação de Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints (para consultas de on-premises para a AWS) e Outbound Endpoints com Resolver Rules compartilhadas via AWS RAM (para encaminhamento de consultas da AWS para on-premises) em uma VPC de Serviços Compartilhados atende à resolução híbrida bidirecional com gestão centralizada.

options.text: Desplegar instancias EC2 con servidores BIND en cada una de las 120 VPCs configurando reenvío mediante iptables. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Administrar servidores BIND en 120 VPCs genera una sobrecarga inmensa de parches, alta disponibilidad y mantenimiento.

options.text: Crear zonas alojadas públicas en Route 53 para example.corp y aws.internal publicando registros A para todos los microservicios internos. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Publicar dominios y direcciones IP privadas en DNS público expone información interna confidencial y vulnera la seguridad corporativa.

options.text: Desplegar Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints en la VPC de Servicios Compartidos para resolver aws.internal y Outbound Endpoints con reglas de reenvío compartidas mediante AWS RAM para resolver example.corp.
options.explanation: Correcto: Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints permite a clientes locales resolver zonas privadas de AWS y Outbound Endpoints con reglas compartidas mediante AWS RAM permite a las VPCs resolver dominios locales sin servidores dedicados.

options.text: Configurar DHCP Option Sets en todas las VPCs apuntando directamente a las IPs de los servidores DNS locales de Active Directory. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Configurar DHCP Option Sets directamente a DNS locales interrumpe la resolución de endpoints internos de AWS y metadatos de instancias.

es.generalExplanation: Implementar Route 53 Resolver Inbound Endpoints (para consultas on-premises a AWS) y Outbound Endpoints con Resolver Rules compartidas mediante AWS RAM en una VPC de Servicios Compartidos centralizada resuelve la resolución híbrida bidireccional.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A multi-tenant SaaS provider uses AWS IAM Identity Center and AWS KMS customer managed keys (CMKs) to encrypt tenant data. The architecture requires that workforce engineers and automated pipeline roles should only be able to decrypt and encrypt data using KMS keys tagged with the same Project and Tenant ID as the user session tags in IAM Identity Center. The security team mandates that this access control must be enforced dynamically using a single centralized KMS key policy without creating separate customer managed keys or modifying key policies whenever new tenants onboard. Which key policy condition satisfies these strict multi-tenant isolation requirements?

options.text: Configure a KMS key policy statement that allows kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey with a Condition block specifying 'StringEquals': {'aws:ResourceTag/TenantID': '${aws:PrincipalTag/TenantID}'}. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Correct: Using the aws:PrincipalTag condition key matched against aws:ResourceTag enables dynamic Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) in KMS, enforcing tenant isolation without per-tenant key policy updates.

options.text: Configure an IAM Permissions Boundary in each member account that adds an explicit Deny for kms:Decrypt when the request does not originate from a specific VPC Endpoint IP address.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Restricting by VPC endpoint IP address does not isolate tenant identities dynamically and requires continuous IP address updates.

options.text: Create separate dedicated AWS KMS multi-region keys for every onboarded tenant and attach an inline IAM policy to each user with hardcoded KMS Key ARNs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Creating individual keys and hardcoding ARNs in IAM policies across hundreds of users and tenants creates severe management overhead that fails the requirement.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda authorizer that intercepts all KMS API calls and validates JWT claims against an Amazon Cognito User Pool before granting access.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS KMS is a foundational cryptographic AWS service that does not support custom external Lambda authorizers in its native API control plane.

questions.generalExplanation: Using Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) in the KMS key policy with the StringEquals condition comparing 'aws:ResourceTag/TenantID' to '${aws:PrincipalTag/TenantID}' dynamically restricts KMS operations to matching tenant session tags without key policy modification.

pt.statement: Um provedor de SaaS multi-tenant utiliza o AWS IAM Identity Center e chaves gerenciadas pelo cliente (CMKs) do AWS KMS para criptografar dados de locatários (tenants). A arquitetura exige que engenheiros e roles de automação só possam criptografar e descriptografar dados usando chaves KMS etiquetadas com o mesmo ID de Projeto e Tenant que as session tags do usuário no IAM Identity Center. questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A pharmaceutical research enterprise hosts a multi-petabyte genomics data lake inside an Amazon S3 bucket within a centralized Data Lake Account. Over 80 separate development and analytics AWS accounts within AWS Organizations need read access to specific dataset prefixes (such as /clinical-trials/ and /genomics-sequencing/). The central security officer establishes two mandatory security rules: first, access must be restricted to originate strictly from internal VPCs via VPC Endpoints with zero internet traversals; second, individual analytics teams must have distinct access permissions managed independently without constantly modifying the central bucket policy. Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to replicate the entire multi-petabyte genomics bucket into 80 dedicated S3 buckets inside each member account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Replicating petabytes of genomic data into 80 separate accounts multiplies storage and cross-account transfer costs by 80x, creating massive cost inefficiency.

options.text: Create Amazon S3 Access Points for the genomics bucket dedicated to each analytics team, configuring the Network origin to Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and specifying the allowed VPC ID for each team.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Access Points allow defining dedicated access hostnames and independent access point policies per team, scoping network origin exclusively to private VPCs.

options.text: Make the central Amazon S3 bucket publicly readable and configure presigned URLs generated by an AWS Lambda function running in each member account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Making sensitive healthcare and genomic buckets public is a critical security vulnerability and violates HIPAA compliance regulations.

options.text: Attach an S3 Access Point Policy to each Access Point that restricts read operations to the specific dataset prefixes and grant permissions to the respective member account IAM roles.
options.explanation: Correct: Access Point policies enable decentralized access governance, allowing granular permissions to be applied per dataset prefix without modifying the central bucket policy.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway in each member account and configure scheduled VTL backups to write data into S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Tape Gateways are for legacy virtual tape archival; they do not provide real-time interactive query access to S3 data lakes.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying Amazon S3 Access Points restricted to VPC Endpoints allows delegating access management to individual datasets with dedicated access point policies. Enforcing access via Gateway/Interface Endpoints ensures all traffic remains entirely on the private AWS network.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: A global banking enterprise is deploying a centralized outbound internet inspection architecture across 90 spoke application VPCs in an AWS Region. Security regulations mandate that all internet-bound egress traffic must be inspected by a scalable cluster of third-party next-generation firewalls (NGFWs) hosted in a central Egress VPC. The design must provide horizontal auto-scaling of firewall appliances, maintain bidirectional TCP flow symmetry without Source NAT, and route traffic from all spoke VPCs to the inspection layer seamlessly. Which combination of steps must the network architect implement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) in the Central Egress VPC and register the third-party firewall instances as targets in the GWLB target group.
options.explanation: Correct: Gateway Load Balancer transparently load balances Layer 3 traffic to fleets of virtual appliances using GENEVE encapsulation, preserving original client and destination IP headers.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in each spoke VPC and configure path-based routing rules that forward all outbound traffic to public NAT Gateways.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Application Load Balancers only handle inbound Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS traffic and cannot act as transparent Layer 3 egress routers for spoke VPCs.

options.text: Create Gateway Load Balancer Endpoints (GWLBE) in dedicated subnets in the Central Egress VPC to receive and forward inspected traffic to NAT Gateways.
options.explanation: Correct: GWLB Endpoints (GWLBE) act as next-hop routing targets in VPC route tables, allowing traffic from the Transit Gateway to flow through firewall appliances before reaching the NAT Gateways.

options.text: Configure VPC Peering connections between all 90 spoke VPCs and the Central Egress VPC with DNS resolution enabled. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering does not support transitive routing (traffic cannot hop from spoke VPC through Egress VPC to the internet via NAT Gateways).

options.text: Enable Proxy Protocol v2 on the Network Load Balancers in each spoke VPC to inject client source IP headers. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Proxy Protocol v2 is an application-layer header mechanism for TCP connections on NLBs, not a routing solution for generic multi-VPC internet egress inspection.

options.text: Connect all spoke VPCs and the Central Egress VPC to an AWS Transit Gateway, configuring spoke route tables with a default 0.0.0.0/0 route pointing to the Transit Gateway.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Transit Gateway acts as the central hub connecting all spoke VPCs, directing their outbound internet default traffic (0.0.0.0/0) to the Central Egress VPC for inspection.

questions.generalExplanation: Designing a centralized egress architecture with third-party firewalls requires: (1) Creating a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) with target groups pointing to the auto-scaled NGFW instances in the Central Egress VPC, (2) Creating Gateway Load Balancer Endpoints (GWLBE) in the Egress VPC subnets, and (3) Connecting spoke VPCs via AWS Transit Gateway with default 0.0.0.0/0 routes pointing to the Transit Gateway, which routes through the GWLB endpoints to NAT Gateways.

Qual combinação de etapas o arquiteto de rede deve implementar? (Escolha três.)

options.text: Implantar um Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) na VPC de Egresso Central e registrar as instâncias de firewall de terceiros como alvos no target group do GWLB.
options.explanation: Correto: O Gateway Load Balancer balanceia tráfego de Camada 3 de forma transparente para frotas de appliances virtuais usando encapsulamento GENEVE, preservando os cabeçalhos IP de origem e destino originais.

options.text: Implantar um Application Load Balancer em cada VPC spoke e configurar regras de roteamento baseadas em caminho que encaminham todo o tráfego de saída para NAT Gateways públicos.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Application Load Balancers só processam tráfego de entrada HTTP/HTTPS de Camada 7 e não operam como roteadores transparentes de egresso de Camada 3.

options.text: Criar Gateway Load Balancer Endpoints (GWLBE) em sub-redes dedicadas na VPC de Egresso Central para receber e encaminhar o tráfego inspecionado para os NAT Gateways.

options.text: Conectar todas as VPCs spoke e a VPC de Egresso Central a um AWS Transit Gateway, configurando as tabelas de rotas das spokes com uma rota padrão 0.0.0.0/0 apontando para o Transit Gateway.

options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los balanceadores de carga de aplicación solo gestionan tráfico entrante de Capa 7 y no funcionan como enrutadores de egreso de Capa 3.

Investigation reveals that the outbound request packet enters the firewall endpoint in AZ-a, but the return response packet is routed to the firewall endpoint in AZ-b, causing stateful inspection drops. Which configuration change must the network architect implement to resolve this issue?

options.text: Enable Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) routing on the Transit Gateway and configure static host routes in each spoke VPC route table. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ECMP balances flows across VPN/Direct Connect paths and does not guarantee symmetric AZ routing on VPC attachments.

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer in each spoke VPC and enable Cross-Zone Load Balancing on all target groups. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ALBs operate at Layer 7 and do not solve Layer 3/4 packet routing asymmetry across Transit Gateway attachments.

options.text: Replace the AWS Network Firewall endpoints with NAT Gateways in each Availability Zone of the spoke application VPCs. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: NAT Gateways only handle outbound internet egress and do not perform stateful deep packet inspection between internal spoke VPCs.

options.text: Enable Transit Gateway Appliance Mode on the VPC attachment that connects the Security VPC to the AWS Transit Gateway. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Correct: Enabling Appliance Mode on the Security VPC Transit Gateway attachment ensures that bidirectional traffic between spokes and the inspection VPC flows symmetrically through the same Availability Zone and firewall ENI.

pt.statement: Uma empresa conecta 60 VPCs de aplicação a um AWS Transit Gateway em us-east-1. Uma VPC de Segurança dedicada hospeda endpoints do AWS Network Firewall com estado em três Zonas de Disponibilidade para inspecionar todo o tráfego entre VPCs. Equipes de aplicação relatam que conexões TCP com estado entre microsserviços em diferentes Zonas de Disponibilidade caem aleatoriamente em horários de pico. A investigação revela que o pacote de requisição de saída entra no endpoint de firewall na AZ-a, mas o pacote de resposta de retorno é roteado para o endpoint na AZ-b, causando descarte na inspeção com estado. Qual alteração de configuração o arquiteto de rede deve implementar para resolver esse problema?

options.text: Habilitar o roteamento Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) no Transit Gateway e configurar rotas estáticas de host na tabela de rotas de cada VPC spoke.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O ECMP balanceia fluxos entre túneis VPN/Direct Connect e não garante roteamento simétrico entre Zonas de Disponibilidade em anexos de VPC.

options.text: Implantar um Application Load Balancer em cada VPC spoke e habilitar o Cross-Zone Load Balancing em todos os target groups. Esta etapa de configuração garante total conformidade com arquiteturas de segurança corporativas e diretrizes do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: ALBs operam na Camada 7 e não resolvem a assimetria de roteamento de pacotes de Camada 3/4 em anexos do Transit Gateway.

options.text: Substituir os endpoints do AWS Network Firewall por NAT Gateways em cada Zona de Disponibilidade das VPCs de aplicação spoke. Esta etapa de configuração garante total conformidade com arquiteturas de segurança corporativas e diretrizes do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorreto: NAT Gateways apenas realizam tradução de endereços para saída à internet e não realizam inspeção profunda de pacotes com estado entre VPCs internas.

options.text: Habilitar o recurso Transit Gateway Appliance Mode no anexo de VPC que conecta a VPC de Segurança ao AWS Transit Gateway. Esta etapa de configuração garante total conformidade com arquiteturas de segurança corporativas e diretrizes do AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Correto: A ativação do Appliance Mode no anexo da VPC de Segurança no Transit Gateway assegura que o tráfego bidirecional entre spokes e a VPC de inspeção passe simetricamente pela mesma Zona de Disponibilidade e ENI do firewall.

pt.generalExplanation: A habilitação do Appliance Mode no anexo de VPC do Transit Gateway que conecta a VPC de Inspeção de Segurança força os fluxos de tráfego bidirecionais de uma sessão a usar a mesma Zona de Disponibilidade e interface ENI.

es.domainName: Dominio 1: Diseñar Soluciones para la Complejidad Organizacional
es.statement: Una empresa conecta 60 VPCs a un AWS Transit Gateway en us-east-1. Una VPC de Seguridad aloja endpoints de AWS Network Firewall en 3 Zonas de Disponibilidad para inspeccionar tráfico inter-VPC. Las conexiones TCP se caen porque la petición entra por AZ-a y la respuesta se enruta por AZ-b. ¿Qué cambio debe implementar el arquitecto de redes para corregir este enrutamiento asimétrico?

options.text: Habilitar enrutamiento ECMP en Transit Gateway y configurar rutas estáticas de host en cada VPC spoke. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: ECMP distribuye flujos entre túneles VPN/Direct Connect y no garantiza simetría de Zonas de Disponibilidad en adjuntos de VPC.

options.text: Desplegar un Application Load Balancer en cada VPC spoke con Cross-Zone Load Balancing habilitado. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los balanceadores de aplicación operan en Capa 7 y no solucionan la asimetría de enrutamiento de Capa 3/4 en Transit Gateway.

options.text: Reemplazar los endpoints de AWS Network Firewall por NAT Gateways en cada Zona de Disponibilidad de las VPCs spoke. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Incorrecto: Los NAT Gateways solo gestionan tráfico saliente a internet y no realizan inspección profunda de tráfico entre VPCs internas.

options.text: Habilitar Transit Gateway Appliance Mode en el adjunto de VPC que conecta la VPC de Seguridad al AWS Transit Gateway. Este paso de configuración garantiza un cumplimiento total con arquitecturas de seguridad corporativas y directrices de AWS Well-Architected Framework.
options.explanation: Correcto: Activar Appliance Mode en el adjunto de la VPC de Seguridad asegura que el tráfico bidireccional pase simétricamente por la misma Zona de Disponibilidad e interfaz ENI del firewall.

es.generalExplanation: Habilitar Appliance Mode en el adjunto de VPC de Transit Gateway de la VPC de Seguridad obliga al tráfico bidireccional de una sesión a pasar por la misma Zona de Disponibilidad e interfaz ENI.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global banking consortium requires a central transactional data store to record inter-bank settlement transactions. Regulatory frameworks mandate that the transaction ledger must be cryptographically verifiable, completely immutable (preventing updates, deletes, or tampering by any administrator or root user), and provide a built-in cryptographic SHA-256 digest hash chain proving historical data integrity for independent regulatory auditors. Which purpose-built database service should the architect deploy?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon DynamoDB table with DynamoDB Streams enabled and replicate transaction events into an Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard DynamoDB tables allow item updates and deletions by authorized IAM users, and S3 versioning does not provide built-in cryptographic SHA-256 transaction verification chains.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster with write-forwarding enabled across multiple AWS Regions and configure an audit trigger that writes to an S3 bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Database administrators can alter triggers, modify underlying table rows, or truncate audit logs, failing the strict immutable cryptographic proof requirement.

options.text: Deploy Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) to store all inter-bank settlement transactions, and utilize the QLDB cryptographic digest API to export proof of data integrity to auditors.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon QLDB has a built-in immutable journal that cannot be updated or deleted by any user, using a Merkle tree and SHA-256 cryptographic hash chain to mathematically verify data integrity.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Timestream database cluster with magnetic storage tiering enabled and configure scheduled AWS Lambda functions to compute MD5 checksums on historical records.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon Timestream is a time-series database optimized for IoT and metrics telemetry, not transactional financial ledgers, and MD5 checksums are vulnerable and lack Merkle tree cryptographic verification.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) is a fully managed ledger database that provides a transparent, immutable, and cryptographically verifiable transaction log owned by a central trusted authority using SHA-256 cryptographic hashing.

pt.domainName: Domínio 2: Projetar Novas Soluções
pt.statement: Um consórcio bancário global exige um armazenamento transacional central para registrar transações de liquidação interbancárias. Frameworks regulatórios exigem que o livro-razão (ledger) de transações seja criptograficamente verificável, completamente imutável (impedindo atualizações, exclusões ou adulterações por qualquer administrador ou usuário root) e forneça uma cadeia de hash criptográfica SHA-256 integrada comprovando a integridade histórica dos dados para auditores regulatórios independentes. Qual serviço de banco de dados sob medida o arquiteto deve implantar?

options.text: Implantar uma tabela do Amazon DynamoDB com DynamoDB Streams ativado e replicar eventos de transação para um bucket do Amazon S3 com versionamento habilitado.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Tabelas padrão do DynamoDB permitem atualização e exclusão de itens por usuários autorizados do IAM, e o versionamento do S3 não fornece cadeias criptográficas integradas de verificação SHA-256.

options.text: Implantar um cluster Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL com write-forwarding ativado em múltiplas Regiões AWS e configurar um trigger de auditoria que grava em um bucket S3.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Administradores de banco de dados podem desativar triggers, modificar linhas de tabelas subjacentes ou limpar logs de auditoria, falhando na exigência de prova criptográfica imutável.

options.text: Implantar o Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) para armazenar todas as transações de liquidação interbancárias e utilizar a API de digest criptográfico do QLDB para exportar comprovações de integridade aos auditores.
options.explanation: Correto: O Amazon QLDB possui um journal imutável integrado que não pode ser alterado ou excluído por nenhum usuário, utilizando uma árvore de Merkle e encadeamento SHA-256 para comprovar matematicamente a integridade dos dados.

options.explanation: Incorreto: O Amazon Timestream é um banco de séries temporais otimizado para telemetria IoT e métricas, não para livros-razão financeiros transacionais, e checksums MD5 são vulneráveis e não fornecem verificação por árvore de Merkle.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A global video streaming platform allows content creators to upload raw 4K video files. The platform must automatically transcode incoming video files into adaptive bitrate HLS formats (1080p, 720p, 480p), store transcoded segments in Amazon S3, and distribute video streams globally via Amazon CloudFront with low latency. Premium video content must be restricted to paying subscribers using time-limited authorization tokens, and the origin S3 buckets must be strictly shielded from direct public internet access. Which serverless architecture fulfills these requirements with the LEAST operational maintenance?

options.text: Deploy an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances running open-source FFmpeg software to poll an S3 bucket, transcode videos into HLS segments, and serve streams directly from public EC2 web servers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed EC2 FFmpeg clusters require complex instance auto-scaling, OS maintenance, patching, and lack global CDN edge caching.

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 event notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function that submits transcoding jobs to AWS Elemental MediaConvert to generate HLS output formats. Store output segments in a private S3 bucket, configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with Origin Access Control (OAC), and enforce CloudFront Signed URLs for subscriber video playback.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Elemental MediaConvert is a serverless broadcast-grade video transcoding service, CloudFront OAC secures private S3 origins, and CloudFront Signed URLs enforce granular, time-limited subscriber authorization.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster running video processing containers that transcode videos and upload them to public S3 buckets configured with S3 website hosting.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running EKS for bursty video transcoding introduces high baseline infrastructure costs, and S3 static website hosting requires public buckets that cannot enforce subscriber authorization.

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic Transcoder configured with manual SQS polling workers, deliver output files to an Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) volume, and stream video content over an AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon Elastic Transcoder is a legacy service, Amazon EFS is not an edge streaming CDN, and Site-to-Site VPN is impractical for public subscriber distribution.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 event notifications trigger AWS Lambda to submit AWS Elemental MediaConvert transcoding jobs. Transcoded HLS outputs are stored in private S3 buckets and distributed globally via Amazon CloudFront using Origin Access Control (OAC) and CloudFront Signed URLs for subscriber authorization.

pt.domainName: Domínio 2: Projetar Novas Soluções
pt.statement: Uma plataforma global de streaming de vídeo permite que criadores de conteúdo enviem arquivos de vídeo 4K brutos. A plataforma deve transcodificar automaticamente os arquivos de vídeo de entrada em formatos HLS de taxa de bits adaptável (1080p, 720p, 480p), armazenar segmentos transcodificados no Amazon S3 e distribuir fluxos de vídeo globalmente via Amazon CloudFront com baixa latência. O conteúdo de vídeo premium deve ser restrito a assinantes pagantes usando tokens de autorização por tempo limitado, e os buckets S3 de origem devem ser estritamente protegidos contra acesso público direto pela internet. Qual arquitetura serverless atende a esses requisitos com a MENOR manutenção operacional?

options.text: Implantar um grupo de Auto Scaling de instâncias Amazon EC2 executando software FFmpeg open-source para consultar um bucket S3, transcodificar vídeos em segmentos HLS e entregar streams diretamente a partir de servidores web EC2 públicos.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Clusters EC2 autogerenciados com FFmpeg exigem auto scaling complexo, manutenção de sistema operacional, aplicação de patches e não possuem cache global de borda via CDN.

options.text: Configurar notificações de eventos do Amazon S3 para invocar uma função AWS Lambda que envia jobs de transcodificação para o AWS Elemental MediaConvert gerando formatos HLS. Armazenar segmentos em um bucket S3 privado, configurar uma distribuição do Amazon CloudFront com Origin Access Control (OAC) e aplicar CloudFront Signed URLs para reprodução de assinantes.
options.explanation: Correto: O AWS Elemental MediaConvert é um serviço serverless de transcodificação de alta qualidade, o CloudFront OAC protege a origem privada no S3 e as URLs assinadas do CloudFront garantem autorização granular e temporária para assinantes.

options.text: Implantar um cluster do Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) executando contêineres de processamento de vídeo que transcodificam vídeos e fazem upload para buckets S3 públicos com hospedagem de site estático.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Executar EKS para processamento de vídeo sob demanda gera altos custos fixos de infraestrutura e hospedagem estática no S3 exige buckets públicos que não suportam controle de autorização de assinantes.

options.text: Usar o Amazon Elastic Transcoder configurado com workers manuais consultando filas SQS, entregar arquivos de saída em um volume do Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) e transmitir vídeo sobre uma AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O Elastic Transcoder é um serviço legado, o Amazon EFS não é uma CDN de borda e a VPN Site-to-Site é inviável para entrega de vídeo a assinantes públicos mundiais.

pt.generalExplanation: Notificações de eventos do Amazon S3 acionam o AWS Lambda para enviar jobs de transcodificação ao AWS Elemental MediaConvert. Saídas HLS transcodificadas são armazenadas em buckets S3 privados e distribuídas globalmente via Amazon CloudFront usando Origin Access Control (OAC) e CloudFront Signed URLs para autorização de assinantes.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: An e-commerce order fulfillment platform receives hundreds of thousands of customer orders per hour. Orders must be processed through payment verification, inventory allocation, and shipment scheduling in strict sequential order per customer account. The architecture must decouple microservices asynchronously, guarantee at-least-once ordered delivery, automatically absorb traffic spikes during seasonal promotions without dropping transactions, and route unparseable poison messages to an administrative Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) after 3 failed attempts. Which architecture fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Send order events directly to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) Standard topic and configure fan-out subscriptions to 10 independent AWS Lambda worker functions.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon SNS Standard topics do not guarantee strict message ordering or deduplication, potentially causing inventory race conditions and out-of-order execution.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) cluster with a persistent MySQL pod and write synchronous REST API integration scripts across all microservices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Synchronous REST integration tightly couples microservices, creating cascading failures during downstream outages and failing the asynchronous decoupling requirement.

options.text: Publish events to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose configured to buffer records for 300 seconds and deliver JSON files into Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Kinesis Data Firehose micro-batching introduces a 5-minute buffering delay, failing the real-time sequential processing requirement for transactional orders.

options.text: Publish order events to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue with the MessageGroupId set to the CustomerID and MessageDeduplicationId enabled. Configure an AWS Lambda function as an event source mapping with a maximum batching window, set maxReceiveCount to 3 on the redrive policy pointing to an SQS FIFO Dead-Letter Queue, and persist state in Amazon DynamoDB.
options.explanation: Correct: SQS FIFO preserves strict message ordering within each MessageGroupId (customer), prevents duplicate messages, supports automated retries with DLQs, and integrates natively with serverless Lambda consumers.

questions.generalExplanation: Publishing customer order events to Amazon SQS FIFO queues with MessageGroupId set to the customer ID, consuming events via AWS Lambda event source mapping with maxBatchingWindow and Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) configuration, and storing order state in Amazon DynamoDB provides decoupled, strictly ordered asynchronous processing.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon DynamoDB Global Table replicated across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-northeast-1 with DynamoDB auto-scaling enabled. options.text: Deploy an Amazon DocumentDB cluster in us-east-1, configure continuous snapshot replication to S3 buckets in other regions, and use Route 53 weighted routing.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Snapshot replication introduces hours of lag and cannot serve real-time sub-10ms leaderboard read/write requests globally.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 Redis cluster in a public subnet in us-east-1 and configure players to connect directly using static Elastic IP addresses.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Single-region EC2 Redis without CDN caching or global replication suffers high international network latency and lacks high availability across continents.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon DynamoDB Global Tables provides fully managed, multi-region active-active database replication with low-latency reads and writes. questions.statement: A global retail conglomerate processes 40 TB of daily transaction logs and clickstream telemetry stored in an Amazon S3 data lake. Data engineering pipelines must run large-scale Apache Spark transformation jobs without managing EC2 server infrastructure or tuning cluster capacity. Transformed datasets must be registered in a centralized metadata catalog and made accessible for interactive SQL analytics by business intelligence teams across multiple AWS accounts using Amazon Redshift Serverless without copying petabytes of data across accounts. Which serverless analytics architecture meets these requirements with the LEAST operational maintenance?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling cluster running open-source Hadoop and Hive, writing output CSV files to Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) gp3 volumes attached to EC2 instances.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed Hadoop and Hive clusters on EC2 require ongoing patching, master node high-availability management, and EBS volumes cannot be shared across multiple accounts.

options.text: Provision a fixed-size Amazon EMR cluster with 50 On-Demand instances, execute Spark jobs, and configure nightly cron scripts to copy transformed files to individual Redshift clusters in every account.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Fixed-size EMR clusters result in substantial idle infrastructure costs and copying petabytes of data nightly to individual Redshift clusters incurs massive storage and egress expenses.

options.text: Use Amazon EMR Serverless to execute Apache Spark data transformation applications on-demand. Catalog transformed Parquet datasets in the AWS Glue Data Catalog on Amazon S3, and use Amazon Redshift Serverless with Redshift Data Sharing to query and share analytical datasets across member accounts without data movement.
options.explanation: Correct: EMR Serverless scales compute resources automatically without managing servers, AWS Glue provides unified metadata cataloging, and Amazon Redshift Serverless Data Sharing enables live, zero-copy data access across AWS accounts.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster with 20 data nodes and configure an AWS Lambda function to stream raw logs into OpenSearch indexes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon OpenSearch Service is optimized for log indexing and search, not large-scale batch Spark transformations and complex relational SQL data warehousing over petabytes of data.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A healthcare technology corporation hosts a core transactional imaging application on a fleet of 200 Linux and Windows Amazon EC2 instances with stateful local databases in the us-east-1 Region. The business continuity office mandates a robust cross-region disaster recovery (DR) solution to eu-west-1 with a Recovery Point Objective (RPO) of less than 30 seconds and a Recovery Time Objective (RTO) of less than 15 minutes. The solution must minimize continuous compute infrastructure costs in the recovery region during normal business operations and support automated non-disruptive DR drill testing. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy 200 identical On-Demand Amazon EC2 instances in eu-west-1 running 24/7, and configure rsync cron jobs over VPC Peering every 10 seconds.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Running 200 active On-Demand instances 24/7 in the recovery region generates massive unnecessary compute costs, and rsync cron jobs over VPC Peering cannot provide sub-30-second block-level database replication consistency.

options.text: Install the AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) Replication Agent on all 200 source EC2 instances in us-east-1, configuring continuous block-level replication to low-cost staging area storage in eu-west-1.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DRS continuously replicates storage volumes at the block level with sub-second RPO using a low-cost, lightweight staging area (inexpensive replication servers and EBS volumes) in the recovery region.

options.text: Configure AWS Backup to take daily AMI snapshots of all 200 instances and copy snapshots to eu-west-1, launching instances manually upon notification.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Daily snapshots result in up to 24 hours of data loss (violating RPO < 30 seconds), and manual launching across 200 servers exceeds the 15-minute RTO.

options.text: Export virtual machine disks as VMDK files into Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Archive buckets every 15 minutes, restoring data using AWS Snowball Edge devices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting VMDKs to Glacier and using physical Snowball devices takes days or weeks to recover, completely violating the 15-minute RTO and 30-second RPO.

options.text: Configure AWS DRS Launch Settings in eu-west-1 with target EC2 instance types, subnets, and security groups, and execute non-disruptive DR drill simulations in an isolated VPC without interrupting ongoing background replication.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS DRS launch settings define pre-configured target compute and networking properties, enabling automated recovery of all 200 instances within minutes during drills or live failover without stopping background replication.

A solução deve minimizar os custos contínuos de infraestrutura de computação na região de recuperação durante a operação normal e suportar testes de simulação de DR automatizados e não disruptivos. options.explanation: Incorreto: Manter 200 instâncias On-Demand ativas 24/7 na região de recuperação gera custos massivos e desnecessários de computação, e o rsync via cron não garante consistência de replicação de banco de dados em nível de bloco sub-30 segundos.

options.text: Instalar o Replication Agent do AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS) em todas as 200 instâncias EC2 de origem em us-east-1, configurando replicação contínua em nível de bloco para uma área de staging de baixo custo em eu-west-1.

options.explanation: Incorreto: Exportar VMDKs para o Glacier e utilizar dispositivos físicos Snowball leva dias ou semanas para recuperação, violando categoricamente o RTO de 15 minutos e RPO de 30 segundos.

questions.domainName: Domain 2: Design for New Solutions
questions.statement: A government agency develops an internal microservices application hosting sensitive citizen data on Amazon ECS in an internal VPC. Frontend applications residing in 50 separate internal agency VPCs must invoke REST APIs securely over private AWS network infrastructure without traversing the public internet. Furthermore, the API tier must enforce rate limiting (throttling), validate incoming JSON payloads, and apply managed web application firewall (WAF) inspection rules against SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks directly on the private API endpoints. Which architecture fulfills these requirements with the HIGHEST security?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway Private REST API with a resource policy restricting access to the Interface VPC Endpoint IDs across the 50 client VPCs. Associate an AWS WAF Web ACL containing AWS Managed Rule sets directly with the API Gateway stage.
options.explanation: Correct: Private REST APIs in API Gateway are only accessible via Interface VPC Endpoints, resource policies restrict access to authorized VPC endpoints, and AWS WAF associates directly with API Gateway stages for Layer 7 inspection.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API in a public subnet, configure mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication with public certificates, and attach an Elastic IP address directly to the API Gateway.
options.explanation: Incorrect: API Gateway HTTP APIs do not support Private endpoint mode inside VPCs and cannot have Elastic IPs attached directly, exposing API traffic to the public internet.

options.text: Deploy self-managed NGINX proxy instances in public subnets in all 50 VPCs, configuring basic HTTP authentication and local modsecurity firewall rules. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed NGINX proxies in public subnets expose private agency networks to the internet and require extensive manual patching and rule management.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each VPC, create VPC Peering between all 50 VPCs, and attach an AWS Shield Advanced protection policy to the NLBs.
options.explanation: Incorrect: NLBs operate at Layer 4 and do not validate JSON schemas or apply AWS WAF Layer 7 inspection rules, and VPC Peering creates high routing management complexity.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon API Gateway Private REST APIs accessed via Interface VPC Endpoints with resource policies, combined with AWS WAF Web ACLs attached directly to the regional API Gateway endpoints, enables private, secure, and protected internal API communication.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A machine learning analytics platform runs on hundreds of private Amazon EC2 GPU instances across 30 VPCs in us-east-1. The instances continuously download training datasets from Amazon S3 and read feature vectors from Amazon DynamoDB tables. Monthly cost reports show $85,000 in NAT Gateway data processing charges. A solutions architect must eliminate all NAT Gateway data processing costs for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB traffic without modifying application code, re-architecting subnets, or adding per-GB data processing fees. Which solution achieves this objective with the LEAST cost?

options.text: Deploy AWS PrivateLink Interface VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in each private subnet across all 30 VPCs. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Interface VPC Endpoints incur hourly endpoint charges and a $0.01 per GB data processing fee, which still results in substantial costs compared to completely free Gateway Endpoints.

options.text: Replace all private subnets with public subnets, assign Elastic IP addresses to all EC2 instances, and disable NAT Gateways. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Placing GPU instances with direct public internet access exposes backend analytics workloads to security risks and violates corporate compliance mandates.

options.text: Configure AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from each VPC to an on-premises proxy server that routes traffic back to AWS via public internet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Routing cloud traffic through on-premises proxies over VPN adds massive latency, egress data transfer costs, and bandwidth bottlenecks.

options.text: Create Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB in all 30 VPCs, and associate the endpoints with all private subnet route tables.
options.explanation: Correct: Gateway VPC Endpoints for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB are provided by AWS at zero additional cost (no hourly charges and no per-GB data processing fees), routing traffic over the AWS network and bypassing NAT Gateways.

questions.statement: A content management enterprise hosts a legacy CMS application running in containerized tasks on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. The application requires access to a shared POSIX file system containing 5 TB of uploaded media assets that must be concurrently accessible by all running container tasks across multiple Availability Zones. During traffic spikes, the ECS service must automatically scale out tasks based on CPU utilization, mounting the shared file system instantly without manual disk provisioning or server configuration. Which architecture satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon EBS io2 Block Express volumes with EBS Multi-Attach enabled, and configure the ECS task definition to attach the EBS volume ID to all Fargate tasks.
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS Multi-Attach is restricted to EC2 instances within a single Availability Zone and is not supported natively by AWS Fargate tasks across multiple Availability Zones.

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with General Purpose performance mode. Configure an EFS Access Point with an enforced POSIX user ID, and configure the Amazon ECS task definition with an EFS volume configuration referencing the access point and task execution role.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon EFS provides serverless, multi-AZ POSIX shared storage that mounts natively on AWS Fargate tasks using EFS Access Points with IAM authorization.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance running Samba Windows File Sharing in a public subnet, mounting the shared drive into ECS tasks using CIFS volume parameters.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed Samba servers create single points of failure, scaling bottlenecks, security vulnerabilities, and require manual maintenance.

options.text: Configure Amazon S3 File Gateway on an EC2 instance in each Availability Zone, and configure Fargate tasks to mount the NFS shares using local boot scripts.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Fargate is a serverless container environment that does not permit running local EC2 boot scripts to mount external Storage Gateway virtual appliances.

questions.generalExplanation: Configuring an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system with EFS access points and referencing the EFS volume directly within the Amazon ECS task definition allows AWS Fargate tasks across multiple Availability Zones to mount shared POSIX storage seamlessly.

questions.statement: A ride-sharing platform records real-time driver GPS locations and trip fare mutations, generating over 120,000 write transactions per second. The application database is hosted on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. During peak commuting hours, high write volume causes severe I/O write contention, buffer cache thrashing, and elevated query response times. The database architecture must be optimized to sustain extreme write throughput, deliver sub-millisecond read latency for live active driver locations, and partition historical trip records automatically by timestamp. Which solution meets these performance requirements with the LEAST latency?

options.text: Increase the Aurora PostgreSQL instance size to db.r6g.16xlarge and create 15 Aurora read replicas across three Availability Zones with read-write splitting. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Aurora read replicas only offload read traffic; adding read replicas does not solve write lock contention or increase master write IOPS capacity.

options.text: Migrate all driver GPS data into Amazon S3 Standard buckets and configure Amazon Athena to execute queries using scheduled AWS Glue crawlers.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon Athena and Glue crawlers have multi-second query latencies and cannot serve real-time transactional driver lookup queries with sub-millisecond requirements.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster as the ultra-low latency in-memory data store for live driver GPS locations with Multi-AZ transactional logging. Implement PostgreSQL declarative table partitioning by timestamp on the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster for completed trip records.
options.explanation: Correct: Amazon MemoryDB for Redis delivers microsecond read/write latencies with Multi-AZ durable transactional log persistence for fast-moving state, while declarative table partitioning in Aurora optimizes large-scale historical queries and vacuuming.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon RDS for MySQL Single-AZ database and configure local cron scripts on EC2 instances to dump database tables to CSV files every 5 minutes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Single-AZ MySQL lacks high availability, lacks sub-millisecond in-memory performance, and cron dumps introduce severe data locking and latency spikes.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying Amazon MemoryDB for Redis as an in-memory primary datastore for live driver locations delivers microsecond read/write latency with Multi-AZ ACID persistence. Implementing native PostgreSQL declarative table partitioning by timestamp on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL handles historical trip archival without write contention.

questions.generalExplanation: Centralizing Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub findings into a delegated Security Account, routing findings via Amazon EventBridge, and invoking AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks that assume cross-account roles to quarantine affected resources delivers automated containment in seconds.

questions.domainName: Domain 3: Continuous Improvement for Existing Solutions
questions.statement: A global insurance enterprise archives 10 PB of historical claim policy documents in Amazon S3. The documents are accessed less than once a year, but when requested for legal discovery, retrieval within 12 hours is acceptable. In response to pending litigation, the corporate legal department mandates that a specific subset of 500,000 policy documents must be placed on indefinite legal hold to strictly prevent deletion or modification by any principal (including account administrators) until the legal hold is explicitly removed. Furthermore, storage costs for the archived files must be minimized. Which storage architecture meets these requirements with the LOWEST cost?

options.text: Store policy documents in S3 Standard, enable S3 Versioning, and create an IAM policy denying s3:DeleteObject to all non-root IAM users. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Standard is expensive for archival storage ($0.023/GB vs $0.00099/GB in Glacier Deep Archive) and IAM policies can be bypassed by administrators with permission management rights.

options.text: Configure S3 Lifecycle rules to transition archived documents to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive. Apply an S3 Object Lock Legal Hold using S3 Batch Operations on the designated 500,000 policy documents.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Glacier Deep Archive provides the lowest-cost cloud storage tier ($0.00099/GB/month with 12-hour Standard retrieval). S3 Object Lock Legal Hold prevents object deletion indefinitely without expiration dates until explicitly removed.

options.text: Transfer policy files to an on-premises Tape Library using AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway and lock virtual tapes in a physical safe.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storing virtual tapes on-premises adds hardware and facility maintenance expenses and prevents automated cloud-based legal retrieval and compliance auditing.

options.text: Enable S3 Object Lock in Governance Mode with a 30-day retention period on an S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access bucket. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance Mode allows users with bypass permissions to delete objects, 30 days is inadequate for multi-year litigation holds, and S3 One Zone-IA lacks multi-AZ resilience.

questions.generalExplanation: Transitioning objects to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive minimizes storage costs ($0.00099 per GB/month), while applying S3 Object Lock with Legal Hold prevents object deletion indefinitely without expiration dates until explicitly removed by authorized legal officers.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A global logistics company plans to migrate 1,200 VMware virtual machines and bare-metal Windows and Linux servers from multiple distributed data centers to Amazon EC2. The migration must execute in waves of 100 servers per weekend. Requirements include non-disruptive continuous data replication, centralized migration tracking across all waves, automated post-launch installation of AWS Systems Manager agents and custom licensing scripts on cutover EC2 instances, and a cutover downtime of under 20 minutes per server. Which solution meets these enterprise migration requirements?

options.text: Export all servers as OVA files, upload them to Amazon S3 using AWS Snowball Edge devices, and call the VM Import/Export CLI operation during each cutover weekend.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exporting OVA files and physically shipping Snowball devices takes weeks, lacks continuous live synchronization, and exceeds the 20-minute cutover window.

options.text: Deploy AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) connectors in all data centers to take scheduled snapshot backups of source VMs into Amazon S3.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS SMS is snapshot-based and deprecated in favor of AWS MGN, which provides real-time continuous block-level replication and automated post-launch script execution.

options.text: Write custom Python scripts using AWS SDK (Boto3) to stop on-premises servers, take dd image copies, transfer images over SFTP, and convert them to EBS snapshots.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Custom dd imaging scripts require stopping source servers for hours, resulting in massive unacceptable downtime and high operational failure risks.

options.text: Install the AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) Replication Agent on all physical and virtual servers. Configure post-launch custom actions in AWS MGN to automatically install the Systems Manager agent and run licensing configuration scripts. Track migration progress across server waves in AWS Migration Hub.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) provides automated continuous asynchronous block-level replication, enables non-disruptive pre-cutover testing, executes post-launch configuration scripts automatically, and integrates with AWS Migration Hub for centralized wave tracking.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) with post-launch custom actions and integrating with AWS Migration Hub provides continuous block-level data replication, automated post-cutover configuration, and centralized wave tracking with minimal cutover downtime.

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert SQL Server schemas, tables, and T-SQL stored procedures to Amazon Aurora MySQL format. options.explanation: Correct: AWS SCT automates schema and code conversion between heterogeneous database engines (SQL Server to MySQL), while AWS DMS with CDC replicates ongoing changes in real time, enabling low-downtime cutover.

options.text: Configure SQL Server Always On Availability Groups to replicate data directly to an Amazon Aurora MySQL read replica over an AWS Direct Connect connection.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SQL Server Always On is a native Microsoft clustering technology that operates exclusively between identical SQL Server instances; it cannot replicate to MySQL engines.

options.text: Deploy AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) to perform block-level replication of the SQL Server VM disks to Amazon Aurora shared storage.
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS MGN is a block-level server lift-and-shift tool; it cannot perform heterogeneous schema conversion from SQL Server relational database to Aurora MySQL.

questions.generalExplanation: Using the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert T-SQL schemas and stored procedures to Aurora MySQL dialect, paired with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) executing a Full Load plus ongoing Change Data Capture (CDC) task, enables near-zero downtime heterogeneous database migration.

questions.statement: An enterprise is modernizing a mission-critical monolithic banking application running in an on-premises data center. The development team is decomposing monolithic functions into microservices running on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate across multiple AWS accounts using the Strangler Fig pattern. Client applications must continue calling a single unified endpoint. Traffic for newly modernized endpoints (such as /accounts and /transfers) must be routed to the new microservices in AWS, while all un-migrated legacy traffic continues routing to the on-premises application without requiring code modifications to the legacy monolith. Which combination of actions should the solutions architect implement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy an AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces environment that connects the on-premises legacy environment and the new microservices AWS accounts through an automated Transit Gateway and API Gateway proxy.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces automatically orchestrates cross-account networking (Transit Gateway and Network Load Balancers) and provisions an API Gateway proxy to manage traffic routing across environments.

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 Weighted Routing to route 50% of incoming DNS queries to the on-premises IP addresses and 50% to the AWS Application Load Balancer.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 Weighted Routing distributes DNS resolution across all traffic randomly; it cannot inspect URL request paths (such as /accounts vs /transfers) to route specific microservice endpoints.

options.text: Create Refactor Spaces services for the containerized microservices and configure path-based route rules matching /accounts and /transfers to point to the ECS Fargate services, while directing default route traffic (/) to the legacy URL endpoint.
options.explanation: Correct: Defining path-based routes in Refactor Spaces transparently intercepts modernized endpoint calls and routes them to AWS microservices while forwarding un-migrated paths to the legacy system.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda@Edge function on Amazon CloudFront to rewrite incoming HTTP requests and forward packets over public internet VPN connections. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Lambda@Edge cannot route requests directly to private RFC 1918 subnets or on-premises networks over private Direct Connect connections without complex public proxies.

options.text: Rewrite all monolithic business logic into Amazon DynamoDB transactional stored procedures and eliminate the legacy database entirely. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value store that does not support relational stored procedures or SQL dialect, requiring destructive refactoring.

questions.generalExplanation: Deploying an AWS Migration Hub Refactor Spaces environment creates an isolated multi-account routing boundary with managed API Gateway and Transit Gateway infrastructure. Defining Refactor Spaces services and route rules with URL path matching allows routing specific endpoints to containerized microservices while routing default traffic to on-premises legacy systems.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A retail banking enterprise runs core banking ledger applications on an IBM z/OS mainframe written in COBOL with CICS transaction processors and DB2 databases. options.text: Use the AWS Mainframe Modernization service with the AWS Blu Age (refactor) pattern to automatically transform COBOL and CICS application code into Java Spring Boot microservices deployed on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, and migrate DB2 relational schemas to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using AWS SCT and AWS DMS.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS Mainframe Modernization with AWS Blu Age automates the refactoring of legacy mainframe applications (COBOL, CICS, VSAM) into containerized Java Spring Boot services deployed on managed AWS compute (ECS/Fargate) with Aurora databases.

options.text: Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance running open-source GnuCOBOL in a public subnet, compiling COBOL files manually and mounting NFS file shares for data storage.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Compiling COBOL with GnuCOBOL on a single EC2 instance lacks automated transformation to Java microservices, introduces single points of failure, and does not modernize CICS transaction monitors.

options.text: Maintain the on-premises mainframe permanently and create AWS Lambda functions that execute telnet terminal screen-scraping 3270 scripts over the internet. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Terminal screen scraping is fragile, introduces high latency, fails security compliance standards, and does not eliminate mainframe operating costs.

options.text: Rewrite all mainframe COBOL applications into Amazon DynamoDB JavaScript stored procedures and host web frontends on Amazon S3 static website hosting. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DynamoDB does not support JavaScript stored procedures or relational banking ledger transactions natively, and rewriting millions of lines manually is high risk.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Mainframe Modernization (Refactor with AWS Blu Age) automatically transforms legacy COBOL/CICS applications into modern Java Spring Boot microservices deployed on Amazon ECS or AWS Fargate backed by Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.

questions.domainName: Domain 4: Accelerate Workload Migration and Modernization
questions.statement: A multinational corporation connects its primary corporate data center to 80 AWS VPCs across multiple AWS Regions using a single 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection. Due to rapid business growth, data transfer bandwidth is nearing 100% capacity. The network engineering team must upgrade connectivity to a resilient 10 Gbps infrastructure with active-active link aggregation, automated link failover without BGP reconvergence delays, and support for adding up to 4 parallel dedicated 10 Gbps connections in a single Link Aggregation Group (LAG). Which hybrid architecture should the network architect deploy?

options.text: Deploy 10 individual 1 Gbps IPsec VPN tunnels across the public internet and configure ECMP routing on a local customer gateway router.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Internet VPN tunnels have bandwidth caps (1.25 Gbps per tunnel), suffer unpredictable internet latency, and cannot aggregate dedicated physical Direct Connect ports into a LAG.

options.text: Provision 80 Private Virtual Interfaces (Private VIFs) on the existing 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection and enable BGP multi-hop routing. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Direct Connect connections support a maximum of 50 Private VIFs and adding virtual interfaces does not increase the underlying 1 Gbps physical port capacity.

options.text: Provision a new Link Aggregation Group (LAG) consisting of dedicated 10 Gbps Direct Connect connections across two distinct Direct Connect locations. Associate the LAG connections with a centralized Direct Connect Gateway using Transit Virtual Interfaces (Transit VIFs) attached to regional AWS Transit Gateways.
options.explanation: Correct: Direct Connect LAG bundles up to four 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps dedicated physical connections into a single logical interface at Layer 2, delivering up to 40 Gbps of aggregated active-active bandwidth with seamless failover and multi-region Transit Gateway routing.

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in each VPC, connecting on-premises SAN arrays over public HTTPS endpoints. This configuration step ensures complete alignment with enterprise security architectures and AWS best practices.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway Volume Gateway is for iSCSI block storage tiering; it does not provide general network layer routing or physical port bandwidth aggregation for VPC workloads.

questions.generalExplanation: Provisioning a 10 Gbps Link Aggregation Group (LAG) on dedicated Direct Connect ports at two distinct Direct Connect locations and associating them with a Direct Connect Gateway provides scalable, highly resilient active-active bandwidth scaling.
